summary.title: CartCo Checkout System - Threat Model
summary.description: Formative STRIDE threat model for CartCo checkout system.

threats.title: Spoofing Identity
threats.description: An attacker steals a customer's session cookies or credentials via cross-site scripting (XSS) or network sniffing to impersonate them.
threats.mitigation: Enforce HTTPS strictly (HSTS), use HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite flags on session cookies, and implement multi-factor authentication (MFA).

threats.title: Repudiation
threats.description: A customer denies placing an unauthorized order or initiating a cart action due to insufficient client-side transaction logging or non-repudiation controls.
threats.mitigation: Maintain secure, immutable server-side audit trails and transaction logs tied to the user’s authenticated session.

threats.title: Spoofing Identity
threats.description: A malicious actor intercepts webhooks or API callbacks by impersonating the payment gateway, sending fake payment success confirmations to trick the application into fulfilling unpaid orders.
threats.mitigation: Validate cryptographic webhook signatures (such as HMAC secrets/tokens) provided by the payment gateway and enforce strict server-to-server TLS certificate validation.

threats.title: Repudiation
threats.description: A customer or the payment provider disputes a transaction, and due to a lack of detailed server-side API response logging, the system cannot prove the exact authorization status received.
threats.mitigation: Log all raw API request and response payloads, transaction IDs, and timestamps from the payment gateway into an immutable audit trail.

threats.title: Spoofing Identity
threats.description: An attacker uses stolen session tokens or credential stuffing to impersonate a legitimate user or administrative account interacting with the web application server.
threats.mitigation: Implement robust authentication mechanisms, secure session management (cryptographically strong tokens, short session timeouts), and multi-factor authentication (MFA).

threats.title: Tampering with Data
threats.description: An attacker exploits input validation vulnerabilities (e.g., SQL injection, cross-site scripting, or parameter pollution) to modify user data, database records, or application files handled by the server.
threats.mitigation: Enforce strict server-side input validation, parameterization, escaping, and parameterized queries/ORMs for all database interactions.

threats.title: Repudiation
threats.description: Users or attackers deny performing malicious actions or unauthorized transactions because the server lacks detailed, immutable audit logs.
threats.mitigation: Implement comprehensive, centralized logging and secure audit trails that capture user IDs, timestamps, and critical actions (such as cart modifications and checkout attempts).

threats.title: Information Disclosure
threats.description: Misconfigured server error messages, unencrypted data transit, or vulnerable endpoints expose sensitive customer data, API keys, or internal system architecture details.
threats.mitigation: Enforce end-to-end TLS encryption, disable verbose stack traces or debug modes in production, and properly secure environment variables and configuration files.

threats.title: Denial of Service
threats.description: Enforce end-to-end TLS encryption, disable verbose stack traces or debug modes in production, and properly secure environment variables and configuration files.
threats.mitigation: Implement rate limiting, Web Application Firewall (WAF) protection, DDoS mitigation services, and resource quotas/timeouts.

threats.title: Elevation of Privilege
threats.description: Flawed access control checks allow a standard authenticated user to execute administrative API endpoints, access other users' cart data, or execute remote code.
threats.mitigation: Implement robust Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) and verify authorization permissions on every server-side request handler before processing.

threats.title: Spoofing Identity
threats.description: An unauthorized service or malicious script attempts to impersonate the web application server when calling checkout and order processing APIs.
threats.mitigation: Implement strict service-to-service authentication using mutual TLS (mTLS), API keys, or JSON Web Tokens (JWT) with digital signatures.

threats.title: Tampering with Data
threats.description: An attacker intercepts or alters transaction payloads (such as item pricing, discounts, or quantities) in transit between the web server and the order processing service.
threats.mitigation: Enforce strict cryptographic integrity checks, data validation, and secure internal communication channels (TLS encryption for all inter-service traffic).

threats.title: Repudiation
threats.description: A user denies completing a financial transaction, or the internal service fails to record a definitive record of an order submission, leading to billing disputes.
threats.mitigation: Implement secure, non-repudiable transaction logging with cryptographic hashing of order states tied to unique timestamps and user identifiers.

threats.title: Information Disclosure
threats.description: Payment transaction details, credit card tokens, or customer billing records are logged insecurely or exposed in plaintext via internal monitoring tools or error responses.
threats.mitigation: Encrypt sensitive financial data at rest and in transit, mask/tokenize credit card data to comply with PCI-DSS standards, and restrict log verbosity.

threats.title: Denial of Service
threats.description: A flood of automated fake checkout requests overwhelms the checkout service, exhausting its processing capacity and preventing legitimate orders from completing.
threats.mitigation: Implement rate limiting, request queuing, and transactional timeouts to gracefully handle traffic spikes and prevent resource exhaustion.

threats.title: Privilege
threats.description: A compromised front-end or low-privileged service account successfully executes privileged backend functions, such as manually approving refunds or bypassing payment verification steps.
threats.mitigation: Implement Principle of Least Privilege (PoLP) across internal service accounts, enforce strict role boundaries, and validate authorization tokens on every transaction API call.

threats.title: Tampering with Data
threats.description: An attacker exploits database vulnerabilities or injection flaws to directly modify prices, user profiles, or cart quantities stored in the database.
threats.mitigation: Use parameterized queries/ORMs, enforce database integrity constraints, and apply strict access control lists (ACLs).

threats.title: Repudiation
threats.description: Malicious database modifications or unauthorized data queries cannot be tracked to a specific user or service due to a lack of database query auditing.
threats.mitigation: Enable comprehensive database activity monitoring (DAM) and immutable audit logging for all write, update, and administrative actions.

threats.title: Information Disclosure
threats.description: Unauthorized access or an unencrypted database backup exposes sensitive user data, PII, and active shopping cart contents.
threats.mitigation: Encrypt all data at rest using robust encryption standards (e.g., AES-256) and enforce encryption in transit for all database connections.

threats.title: Denial of Service
threats.description: Maliciously crafted queries or database connection flooding exhausts database resources, preventing the web app from reading or writing user carts.
threats.mitigation: Implement query performance tuning, connection pooling limits, resource throttling, and automated database failover clusters.

threats.title: Tampering with Data
threats.description: An attacker with compromised credentials or database injection access modifies historical order records, alters transaction amounts, or deletes completed order logs.
threats.mitigation: Implement strict database access controls (Principle of Least Privilege), use parameterized queries to prevent SQL injection, and maintain immutable, append-only transaction logs.

threats.title: Repudiation
threats.description: The database lacks sufficient transaction logging or audit trails, making it impossible to prove who accessed, modified, or deleted sensitive order history records.
threats.mitigation: Enable comprehensive database audit logging (capturing who, what, when, and from where records were modified or accessed) and store logs in a secure, write-once-read-many (WORM) storage.

threats.title: Information Disclosure
threats.description: Sensitive customer order details, billing histories, and personally identifiable information (PII) stored in the database are exposed via unencrypted storage or unauthorized data dumps.
threats.mitigation: Encrypt all data at rest using strong industry-standard encryption (e.g., AES-256), enforce column-level encryption for sensitive fields, and restrict direct administrative access.

threats.title: Denial of Service
threats.description: A high volume of complex analytical queries or resource-intensive database transactions exhausts database connection pools and CPU resources, causing service failure.
threats.mitigation: Implement connection pooling limits, query timeout configurations, rate limiting on reporting endpoints, and database resource provisioning/scaling
